text:
maria.garcia: Heads-up — storage-audit alert flagged a few DB snapshot objects in s3://redwood-db-backups/2026/03/ without SSE-KMS headers. Not sure if migration or a policy drift.
jonathan.sre: Which object keys?
maria.garcia: Found: 2026-03-18/postgres-prod-base-20260318.dump, 2026-03-19/pg-snap-20260319.tar, 2026-03-20/pg-snap-20260320.tar. CloudTrail shows PutObject events missing x-amz-server-side-encryption, caller = backup-service-role@redwood-prod.
kevin.infra: backup-service-role normally blocked by bucket policy. Could be a cross-bucket CopyObject that omitted SSE. Any CopyObject events in CloudTrail near those times?
anya.devex: Pulled CloudTrail quickly: CopyObject at 2026-03-19T02:12:08Z from s3://temp-migrations, and a PutObject at 2026-03-20T03:01:22Z. Both used aws-sdk v1.11 without SSE param.
incident-bot: INC-2026-0319 created: s3-unencrypted-snapshots. Initial severity P2 — assigned to #eng-security, paging enabled.
jonathan.sre: Quick triage: confirm if these are logical dumps (plaintext) or encrypted EBS exports. If logical pg_dump tarballs, then lack of SSE = plaintext at rest.
maria.garcia: Confirmed: pg dumps and basebackup tarballs — plaintext if not encrypted by S3.
kevin.infra: Proposed immediate actions:
- Apply bucket policy Deny for PutObject/CopyObject when s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption != "aws:kms" (staging first)
- Audit KMS grants for principal activity in the window
- Temporarily revoke backup-service-role KMS grants until it uses SSE param
- Identify and re-ingest affected objects encrypted with KMS from source or regenerate
anya.devex: Running S3 inventory on the prefix now.
maria.garcia: Also search for GetObject events for those keys to check if anyone downloaded them.
jonathan.sre: I'll grep CloudTrail for GetObject where requestParameters.key matches those prefixes.
anya.devex: Inventory quick output: the three objects present; head-object responses show no ServerSideEncryption header. I've tagged them audit:unencrypted=true for tracking.
maria.garcia: Added alert correlation ID alert-2026-1192 to the incident evidence. Please include CloudTrail event IDs too.
incident-bot: Note added to INC-2026-0319 by maria.garcia
jonathan.sre: CloudTrail grep shows a GetObject for 2026-03-19/pg-snap-20260319.tar at 2026-03-21T10:44:12Z by analytics-job@redwood-prod (assumed role analytics-runner).
anya.devex: Confirmed from analytics team: they fetched that snapshot for an offline data validation job, then deleted local copy.
maria.garcia: We need to check whether analytics-runner had permission to assume backup-service-role or had independent access. Also verify network egress for that instance.
kevin.infra: KMS key policy currently grants backup-service-role and analytics-role. Important: if object had no SSE header, KMS wasn't involved for PutObject — S3 stored plaintext. So KMS grants don't change whether object was encrypted. But we should still audit which principals had access to the bucket and any GET events.
jonathan.sre: Network/egress audit: no transfers to external IPs tied to analytics-runner in that timeframe. Looks internal. Lowering severity to P3 for now but keep incident open.
maria.garcia: Remediation checklist (proposed):
- Enforce bucket deny policy for non-SSE uploads (kevin)
- Full inventory of backup buckets and report missing SSE headers (anya)
- Re-ingest or regenerate missing objects under SSE-KMS (backup team)
- Consider CMK rotation or create new CMK for future backups (security + infra)
- Add CI/CD preflight in backup pipeline to fail if SSE header missing (eng-runtime)
- Blameless postmortem and tabletop drill (maria)
anya.devex: I'll implement a daily artifact check that opens a ticket for any backup object missing SSE-KMS; PR WIP: github.com/redwood/repo/pull/4586
kevin.infra: Bucket policy snippet I plan to test in staging:
```json
{
  "Sid": "DenyUnEncryptedUploads",
  "Effect": "Deny",
  "Principal": "*",
  "Action": ["s3:PutObject","s3:CopyObject"],
  "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::redwood-db-backups/*",
  "Condition": {"StringNotEquals": {"s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption": "aws:kms"}}
}
```
kevin.infra: Note: CopyObject requires SSE params on the copy request or it will be blocked by this deny. We'll need to ensure migration tooling sets SSE for cross-bucket copies.
maria.garcia: Also add an S3 Event Notification to fire OBJECT_CREATED events to a lambda that validates the ServerSideEncryption header and tags non-compliant objects for automated tracking.
jonathan.sre: I'm adding the CloudTrail detection query to the SRE runbook. Example SQL for our CT logs: 
SELECT eventTime, eventName, userIdentity.principalId, requestParameters.key FROM cloudtrail_logs WHERE eventName IN ('PutObject','CopyObject','GetObject') AND requestParameters.bucketName = 'redwood-db-backups' AND eventTime BETWEEN '2026-03-18' AND '2026-03-22';
kevin.infra: For KMS key handling: recommend creating a new CMK and using it for future backups. Do not delete old CMK immediately; retire after 6 months if not used. Update aliases and grants accordingly.
maria.garcia: Communication: I'll notify Compliance and Legal with the timeline and evidence we have (no external download observed). Draft notice in 2 hours.
anya.devex: Dropping the list of object ARNs and CloudTrail event IDs into the incident thread in 15m.
jonathan.sre: Postmortem drill suggestion: quarterly tabletop simulating an unencrypted migration bucket copying into backups; validate alerting, runbook, and postmortem flow.
maria.garcia: +1. Also add unit tests in backup pipeline mocks to assert PutObject calls include SSE header; fail CI if not.
kevin.infra: Also review third-party object stores (GCS, DO Spaces) to ensure parity of SSE enforcement across providers.
incident-bot: INC-2026-0319 status updated: investigation -> remediation
maria.garcia: Summary: incident INC-2026-0319 (now P3), no external exfil evidence, deny policy to be tested in staging, inventory + reupload in progress, KMS rotation under review, postmortem scheduled. Next update in 2 hours or sooner if we find external GetObject events.
